after.title: Art direction: Hearth & Thread (reference = concept picture)
after.text:
Cozy cottage at night with rain on the window. You play against Granny Owl, who knits across the table.

- Owl = the AI's tells: sleepier after each draw (spectacles slip, yawn); she sets down her teacup before her L5 Ward.
- L2 rock = a sleeping cat; Shatter shoos it off.
- Animation: the scissors snip and the button pops off; the thread tugs and the stitch glides; a win sews a golden line; a loss unravels and goes grey; Second Wind re-knits.

- Add tests: shield blocks Shatter's placement; winning Ward needs no shieldCell; ward:2 decrements once and yields one action per shield cell (no duplicate branches: legalActions enumerates distinct actions, not power copies).
- BUG in test 'Ward cannot remove the last legal reply': X at 6 completes column 0 (cells 0,3,6), so a winning Ward is legal and the assertion fails. Change cell 3 to 'O' (or 0) so no win exists.
- AI search capped ~6 plies, root budget ~300ms; prune X power branches beyond ply 2. Fallback to best-so-far on timeout. No pause over ~0.5s.

after.title: Implementation handoff: reducer source
after.text:
rules.mjs v2 and rules.test.mjs v2 are flowchart source cards, unexecuted. Copy into a JS workspace and run node --test. The reducer owns Position only; the controller owns drafts, boards, Second Wind, AI policy and Heat. Heat counts placement events only.

Rulings:
- Search uses isLegal(s,a) plus an unchecked apply. The public API keeps the full check.
- AI: iterative deepening with alpha-beta, max 6 plies, ~300ms. X power branches are searched through ply 4, plain placements after that. The cutoff eval values inventory and shields. Consecutive Slides are allowed.
- Worker requests carry a position revision. On timeout, return the best move from the last completed depth for that same revision. The controller drops any reply whose revision doesn't match, so a stale move can never be played.

summary: edited section “What we're building”

before.title: What we're building
before.text:
Roguelite tic-tac-toe vs an AI. Juicy: dynamic colors, animations, WebAudio sound. Single-page web, no assets. Five mechanics, no more.

1. Ladder: 5 levels, max 3 boards each (a draw burns one, no draft, powers kept; out of boards = run over). X line clears the level + draft. O line = run over, except one Second Wind per run: cancels that loss only (replays a fresh board; no extra board, draft or Heat; counts as the same attempt). L5 clear = victory + score. Run ~8 min.
2. Powers: Shatter, Slide, Ward. Each includes your placement; 1 per turn; hold 3; preview before confirming. Start: pick 1 of 3. Draft 1 of 3 per cleared level (swap or skip at cap).
3. AI blunder rate: L1 80%, L2 40%, L3 25%, L4 10%, L5 0% (minimax with powers/shields in search). Each draw adds +10% for the rest of the level (visible hesitation). L1-L3: blunder rolls first and may miss a win/block. L4-L5: take an immediate win first, blunder only on the follow-up.
4. Level setups (never stack; reset per board, keep inventory):
 L1 empty, X starts.
 L2 rock top-left (blocks cells and lines; Shatter can remove it).
 L3 seeds X top-left, O bottom-right, X starts (Slide shines).
 L4 empty, O starts (hardest board).
 L5 O owns one Ward per board: shield on one empty cell, chosen and displayed (with a distinct shape) before X's turn, blocks X placement into it, expires after X's action, must leave X a legal move.
5. Heat (cosmetic only): +1 per placement, +2 on win, cap 10, reset per board. Drives palette, music layers, particles, power shockwave size. Marks stay readable at Heat 10.

Powers: Shatter = remove one O (or rock), place X elsewhere. Slide = move one X, then place X; lines resolve after. Ward = place X, shield one empty cell from the next AI move; must leave AI a legal reply unless you win.
A winning player action ends the board before the AI replies. Draw = no playable empty cells, no line.

Loss beat (presentation, not a mechanic): losing O line pulses, last two moves replay in 1s slow-mo, Heat colors drain to grey with a falling tone, board shatters. Then a card: level reached, score vs best, and one-tap "Again" (new run, under 1s). Second Wind instead rewinds the shards back together with a rising chime.
Cut: Echo, Rewind, charge economy, shifting corners, O-center seed.

before.title: What we're building
before.text:
Roguelite tic-tac-toe vs an AI. Juicy: dynamic colors, animations, WebAudio sound. Single-page web, no assets. Five mechanics, no more.

1. Ladder: 5 levels, max 3 boards each (a draw burns one, no draft, powers kept; out of boards = run over). X line clears the level + draft. O line = run over, except one Second Wind per run: cancels that loss only (replays a fresh board; no extra board, draft or Heat; counts as the same attempt). L5 clear = victory + score. Run ~8 min.
2. Powers: Shatter, Slide, Ward. Each includes your placement; 1 per turn; hold 3; preview before confirming. Start: pick 1 of 3. Draft 1 of 3 per cleared level (swap or skip at cap).
3. AI blunder rate: L1 80%, L2 40%, L3 25%, L4 10%, L5 0% (minimax with powers/shields in search). Each draw adds +10% for the rest of the level (visible hesitation). L1-L3: blunder rolls first and may miss a win/block. L4-L5: take an immediate win first, blunder only on the follow-up.
4. Level setups (never stack; reset per board, keep inventory):
 L1 empty, X starts.
 L2 rock top-left (blocks cells and lines; Shatter can remove it).
 L3 seeds X top-left, O bottom-right, X starts (Slide shines).
 L4 empty, O starts (hardest board).
 L5 O owns one Ward per board: shield on one empty cell, chosen and displayed before X's turn, blocks X placement into it, expires after X's action, must leave X a legal move.
5. Heat (cosmetic only, shown as the HEARTH gauge): +1 per placement, +2 on win, cap 10, reset per board. Drives palette, music layers, particles, power effect size. Marks stay readable at Heat 10.

Powers: Shatter = remove one O (or rock), place X elsewhere. Slide = move one X, then place X; lines resolve after. Ward = place X, shield one empty cell from the next AI move; must leave AI a legal reply unless you win.
A winning player action ends the board before the AI replies. Draw = no playable empty cells, no line.

Loss beat (presentation, not a mechanic): the losing O line pulses, the last two moves replay in 1s slow-mo, the quilt unravels and goes grey with a falling tone. Then a card: level reached, score vs best, one-tap "Again" (new run in under 1s). Second Wind re-knits the threads with a rising chime instead.
Cut: Echo, Rewind, charge economy, shifting corners, O-center seed.

after.title: QA paper run L1→L5: L5 can't be won
after.notes:
Traced by hand against rules v2 + controller v2. L1 and L2 clear on board 1. L3 clears fast with a seeded Slide. Two breaks:

1) L5 is unwinnable. X starts vs a 0%-blunder minimax that searches X's powers = every board draws, so the +10%-per-draw tilt becomes the ONLY win condition (30% by board 3). Skill stops mattering at the finale. Fix: O's Ward costs her the turn — she sets down the teacup instead of stitching. X gets real tempo against a perfect defence, and the tell is already in the art.
2) L4's likeliest death is draw-exhaustion, and Second Wind only cancels O lines. The save never fires where the run actually ends.
Minor: at L3 the player already holds 3 powers, so level 3 is the softest board in the run — that's the right place for the fun, wrong place for the curve.

before.title: What we're building
before.text:
Roguelite tic-tac-toe vs an AI. Juicy: dynamic colors, animations, WebAudio sound. Single-page web, no assets. Five mechanics, no more.

1. Ladder: 5 levels, max 3 boards each (a draw burns one, no draft, powers kept; out of boards = run over). X line clears the level + draft. Second Wind (once per run) cancels the first run-ending event of either kind (an O line or the last board burned) and grants one fresh board on that level (1 heart, no draft, no Heat). L5 clear = victory. Run ~8 min.
 Score: +100 per level cleared, +50 per heart left at the clear, +25 per power spent this level. The card shows score vs best.
2. Powers: Shatter, Slide, Ward. Each includes your placement; 1 per turn; hold 3; preview before confirming. Start: pick 1 of 3. Draft 1 of 3 per cleared level (swap or skip at cap). The L4 to L5 draft can't be skipped while you hold 0 powers.
 Core tension: spend powers for score now, or save them, because L5 is only winnable with a power in hand.
3. AI blunder rate: L1 80%, L2 40%, L3 25%, L4 10%, L5 0% (minimax with powers/shields in search). Each draw adds +10% for the rest of the level (visible hesitation). L1-L3: blunder rolls first and may miss a win/block. L4-L5: take an immediate win first, blunder only on the follow-up.

 L1 empty, X starts.
 L2 rock top-left (blocks cells and lines; Shatter can remove it).
 L3 seeds X top-left, O bottom-right, X starts (Slide shines).
 L4 empty, O starts (hardest board).

Powers: Shatter = remove one O (or rock), place X elsewhere. Slide = move one X, then place X; lines resolve after. Ward = place X, shield one empty cell from the next AI move; must leave AI a legal reply unless you win.

author: claude
summary: edited card “QA paper run: L5 verdict = measure it”

before.title: QA paper run: L5 verdict = measure it
before.notes:
Retracting "L5 is unwinnable". Foreman's line checks out by hand and so does mine — but not for the reason given. The win isn't the first fork; it's the recursion. After Shatter X holds three marks, and whichever single mark O blocks, adding one more X creates a *second* one-cell threat, so O faces two threats with one placement and one shield. X wins by arithmetic, not by cleverness.

Example (mine, on the fixture card): X 0,4 / O 5,8. Shatter 8, place 1 → X 0,1,4 forks 2 and 7. O blocks 2 and shields 7; X plays 3, threatening 6; O blocks 6; shield on 7 expires; X plays 7 and wins column 1-4-7.

What stays open, and only the worker answers it: does a perfect O avoid ever letting X reach three marks on a fork shape, and does the shipped 6-ply cap see the recursion at all. If the win only appears inside the horizon, L5's "0% minimax" is an artifact and the level is fake. Instrument: seed 200 L5 boards with 3 powers, target 55-70% clear. Above 85% the finale is a formality; below 40% it is a wall.

That's one line, not a proof; verify in the worker. Fix: can't skip the L4 to L5 draft at 0 powers. Ward-costs-turn rejected.
